q1: <!-- comment --> is the HTML comment syntax. Everything between <!-- and --> is ignored by the browser's rendering engine but visible in page source.
q2: < and > and & must be escaped. These three characters are special in HTML. < becomes <, > becomes >, and & becomes & to prevent parsing errors.
q3: A copyright symbol ©. © is the named HTML entity for ©. You can also use the numeric form ©.
q4: A non-breaking space.   inserts a space that also prevents a line-wrap at that position — useful for keeping values like '10 km' together on one line.
q5: An ampersand & is rendered. & is the safe way to display a literal & character in HTML without starting an entity sequence.
q6: No — nested comments break parsing. The first --> closes the outermost comment, so text after it is treated as regular HTML content.
q7: They collapse to a single space. HTML normalises runs of whitespace into one space during rendering. Use   or CSS to preserve extra spacing.
q8: No — but they ARE visible in page source. Comments don't render on screen, but anyone can view them via View Source or DevTools, so never put passwords or secrets in comments.
q9: < represents <. Numeric entities use the decimal Unicode code point. 60 = <, 62 = >, 38 = &, 160 = non-breaking space.
q10: To prevent the browser from interpreting them as tag markers. Writing a raw < in content can confuse the parser into thinking a new tag is starting, causing broken markup.
